policy: Nothing on this page is implemented. Each item is a proposal with the evidence that motivates it, what it costs, what it risks, and the decision it unblocks. A reviewer sets state to approved/rejected/deferred; only approved items may be implemented, and any implementation must change the named files and nothing else.
review_rule: A suggestion may not be implemented while its blocking question is unanswered. The blocking question id is in the `blocked_by` field and resolves to the questions register.
generated_from: measurements produced by this hub's build (data/*.json) plus the official sources in data/sources.json

suggestions.title: Ingest a timestamped odds archive before any opening/closing claim is made
suggestions.evidence: The schedules feed stores ONE price per market and no sampling time, so 7,103 of 7,103 snapshots are graded `unattributed_single_observation`. Only 2021 has a separate early snapshot, and the publisher does not document or date it.
suggestions.proposal: Add a fetch step for a source that publishes an explicit timestamp per price (open and close), then re-grade every snapshot. Until then the price page keeps the `unattributed` grade and the opening-number study stays limited to n=67.
suggestions.impact: HIGH - without it, line-move signals and closing-line value cannot be measured at all.
suggestions.cost: Medium: one new feed, one schema change, one re-run. Licensing may cost money.
suggestions.risk: A cheap feed can be a stale or unofficial one; grading it `verified` would be worse than the current honest blank.
suggestions.unblocks: DA-S01 (market-move fade), per-bet CLV, the demotion rule DM-1, and any claim about beating the close.

suggestions.title: Refresh the results feed in-season, weekly, and diff it against NFL.com
suggestions.evidence: The committed snapshot is frozen at gameday 2026-11-01. The official Week 10 Thursday game (WAS 24, NYG 21) is published on NFL.com but absent from the snapshot, so the current slate cannot be scored from the committed data.
suggestions.proposal: Run the existing build-verify/data-pipeline schedule, then have this hub re-fetch the schedules feed and re-reconcile the most recent completed week against the official schedule page, publishing a per-week diff count.
suggestions.impact: HIGH - a stale results feed makes every backtest and ROI figure describe history, not the current season.
suggestions.cost: Low: the workflow already runs; this adds one reconcile step.
suggestions.risk: Official pages are hand-read here; an automated fetch of nfl.com may be blocked, in which case the diff must stay manual and be labelled so.
suggestions.unblocks: Scoring the current slate (Week 10), and any 'live' strategy status.

suggestions.title: Stop publishing the rating model as a market competitor; publish it as a signal generator
suggestions.evidence: Walk-forward, the model's side error is worse than the market's in every evaluated season (2023: 10.65 vs 9.90 pts; 2024: 11.18 vs 9.61; 2025: 11.13 vs 9.72; 2026: 9.92 vs 9.48), and its ATS win rate on its own side is 47.8% / 48.9% / 43.8% / 45.0%.
suggestions.proposal: Keep the fair/market/difference columns (they are the useful output) but label the model explicitly as a benchmark-relative signal generator, not a line-beating model. Remove any 'we originate better lines' framing that the data does not support.
suggestions.impact: MEDIUM - protects the reader from acting on an overstatement; costs nothing statistically.
suggestions.cost: Low: wording and one verdict field.
suggestions.risk: Under-selling: a future model could beat the market, and the label must then be re-earned by the same walk-forward test.
suggestions.unblocks: A clean basis for the leaderboard's benchmark column.

suggestions.title: Add a price-aware edge filter so 'difference' becomes an actionable number
suggestions.evidence: The difference column currently compares the model's fair line to the market's number. Without a price per side, a 3-point difference on a -115 price is not the same bet as on -105, and 1,584 of DA-S08's 5,909 opportunities carry no price at all.
suggestions.proposal: Publish, per originated game, the break-even price implied by the model's probability, next to the actual price where one exists, and mark the bet 'positive' only when the price clears break-even.
suggestions.impact: HIGH - converts a descriptive difference into a decision rule with a cost.
suggestions.cost: Low: arithmetic only, using prices already present.
suggestions.risk: A positive-EV number computed from an uncalibrated model will look more authoritative than it is; it must carry the model's own error bar.
suggestions.unblocks: A defensible staking rule and the price-discipline gate DA-G7.

suggestions.title: Run the depth and injury build in CI so replacement depth stops being blocked
suggestions.evidence: This sandbox cannot reach GitHub release assets (TLS reset on every feed), so snap counts are absent and `can_answer_how_deep_is_the_replacement` is false. The repository already ships a workflow that fetches these on a runner successfully.
suggestions.proposal: Add .github/workflows/decision-arena.yml that runs fetch_inputs.py then the full build on ubuntu-latest and commits the derived JSON only. The depth page then upgrades itself from BLOCKED to MEASURED with no code change.
suggestions.impact: HIGH - the depth question is a stated requirement and is currently unanswerable.
suggestions.cost: Low: one workflow file, already written.
suggestions.risk: A third-party feed outage would fail the job; the job is fail-closed so the last good data stays published rather than being replaced with blanks.
suggestions.unblocks: Replacement-depth measurement, position-thinness tables, injury-adjusted signals.

suggestions.title: Define a 'depth lost' index before measuring injury impact
suggestions.evidence: The official report lists 66 players Out across 28 clubs for Week 10, but carries no depth rank, so 'the starter is out' and 'the 4th string is out' are indistinguishable in the official data.
suggestions.proposal: Pre-commit a formula: depth_lost = sum over Out/Doubtful players of 1/(depth_rank), by side of ball, and publish it per club-week next to the raw report. Fix the formula before looking at any outcome variable.
suggestions.impact: MEDIUM - makes injury impact comparable across clubs and testable.
suggestions.risk: Any weighting is a choice; publishing the formula first prevents choosing it after seeing results.
suggestions.unblocks: An injury-and-depth signal family, and the user's starter/backup requirement.

suggestions.title: Price prop combos only after a prop-price feed exists; do not back-fit them
suggestions.evidence: Receptions vs receiving yards correlate at r = 0.80 (n = 45,315) and QB yards vs WR1 at 0.55 (n = 5,893), but no committed feed holds a historical player-prop price, so DA-S10/DA-S11 have n = 0 priced bets and are EXECUTION_BLOCKED.
suggestions.proposal: Keep the measured correlations published. When a prop-price archive exists, price the combos at the measured joint rate and run them through the same ten gates, at the same sample floor as singles.
suggestions.impact: MEDIUM - unlocks a whole family without inventing results now.
suggestions.cost: High: prop price archives are expensive or unavailable.
suggestions.risk: Prop prices move fastest and are most often limited; a backtest on quoted prices may not be executable at those stakes.
suggestions.unblocks: DA-S10, DA-S11, and the prop half of the competition.

suggestions.title: Raise the sample window instead of lowering the gate
suggestions.evidence: Every strategy fails gate DA-G2 (n >= 300 graded and n >= 100 priced). The best-populated family is DA-S08 with 4,325 graded and 2,741 priced; the worst is DA-S12 with 157. Nine seasons of prices exist at most, and only 73.2% of spread legs carry one.
suggestions.proposal: Do not weaken DA-G2. Instead extend the priced history (more seasons with prices, SUG-01) and pool variants that are pre-specified as one family rather than counted as separate tests.
suggestions.risk: Pooling variants raises power but hides heterogeneity; the pooled rule must be registered before scoring.

suggestions.title: Decide whether the competition pays money or only ranks
suggestions.evidence: The reward schedule publishes three tiers and `prize_pool: null` with status UNFUNDED, because no funded pool, sponsor, or currency exists anywhere in the repository.
suggestions.proposal: Either (a) fund a pool with a named source and publish the amount and the rules, or (b) rename 'rewards' to 'promotion tiers' and stop implying a prize. Publishing a number without funding it is the one option to avoid.
suggestions.impact: MEDIUM - affects whether the competition is an incentive or a ranking.
suggestions.risk: (a) creates payment obligations and likely regulatory questions; (b) may reduce the incentive to contribute.
suggestions.unblocks: Honest reward language and the leaderboard's headline.

suggestions.title: Wire the demotion gate to an automatic weekly evaluation
suggestions.evidence: Six demotion triggers (DM-1..DM-6) and two promotion rules are defined and published, but nothing currently evaluates them on a schedule; with 0 live strategies the rules are untested in operation.
suggestions.proposal: Run the demotion evaluation in the same weekly job as the results refresh, write the state transitions to a log, and publish 'stale' when a strategy stops receiving prices (DM-6).
suggestions.impact: MEDIUM - the difference between a rule and a ritual.
suggestions.risk: An automated demotion on a thin sample could churn; the minimum-bet floors prevent that and must be enforced in code.
suggestions.unblocks: The user's 'define a demotion gate' requirement becoming operational rather than documentary.
